summary: Defines textual conventions, shared data type definitions, for managing Virtual Private Networks with network management protocols. These building blocks are used by other management information base modules. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: When many forms need the same kind of answer, you define a standard box once. This memo defines those standard boxes for managing private network links.

questions: what is a textual convention in snmp
how long is a vpn identifier
subtitle: Shared SNMP data types for naming a VPN with a 7-byte Global VPN Identifier.

tldr.problem: Several VPN-related MIB modules need to refer to a VPN by its identifier, and each would otherwise have to define the same data type separately.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines the VPN-TC-STD-MIB module with two textual conventions: VPNId, a 7-octet string, and VPNIdOrZero, which also allows a zero-length string.
tldr.outcome: Other MIB modules can import these types to identify a VPN consistently. The module defines no managed objects, so it has no security impact by itself.

today: RFC 4265 is a Proposed Standard, published in November 2005. No RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Purpose of the Memo
sections.content:
This memo defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for use with network management protocols in the Internet community. In particular, it defines Textual Conventions used in Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) and in IETF VPN-related MIBs.

A textual convention is a reusable data type definition. Defining the VPN ones in one place means other MIB modules can import them instead of repeating the definitions.
sections.eli5: Instead of every form inventing its own box for the answer, this memo draws one shared box that everyone can copy.

sections.title: The Management Framework
sections.content:
The memo points to section 7 of RFC 3410 for an overview of the Internet-Standard Management Framework. Managed objects are accessed through a virtual information store, the MIB, generally using the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP). Objects in the MIB are defined using the Structure of Management Information (SMI).

The module in this memo is compliant with SMIv2, described in STD 58: RFC 2578, RFC 2579 and RFC 2580.
sections.eli5: Network gear keeps its facts in a big shared rulebook. SNMP is the way to read it, and this memo adds a few new rules to the book.

sections.title: The VPN Identifier Types
sections.content:
The VPN-TC-STD-MIB defines a textual convention for the Global VPN Identifier, or VPN-ID, as specified in RFC 2685. The purpose of a VPN-ID is to uniquely identify a VPN. It MUST be 7 octets in length, and SHOULD be made of a 3 octet Organizationally Unique Identifier (OUI) that identifies the VPN Authority, followed by a 4 octet value assigned by that authority to identify the VPN within the context of the OUI.

Two types result. VPNId is an OCTET STRING (SIZE (7)). VPNIdOrZero extends it to OCTET STRING (SIZE (0 | 7)), so it also permits a zero-length string. The meaning of the zero-length value is object-specific and must be defined in the description of any object that uses this syntax. The RFC gives as examples situations where none or all VPN IDs need to be referenced.
sections.eli5: A VPN's name tag is 7 bytes: 3 for who handed it out and 4 for which network it is. A second kind of tag also allows a blank one, whose meaning each form decides.

sections.title: The Module Definition
sections.content:
The module is named VPN-TC-STD-MIB and its identity is vpnTcMIB, placed at { mib-2 129 }. It imports MODULE-IDENTITY and mib-2 from SNMPv2-SMI and TEXTUAL-CONVENTION from SNMPv2-TC. It is a product of the PPVPN working group and subsequently the Layer 3 Virtual Private Networks (L3VPN) Working Group.

The only revision listed is dated 15 November 2005, described as the initial version, published as RFC 4265. Both textual conventions have STATUS current.
sections.eli5: The memo is mostly the official wording of the two boxes, written in the special language used for these rulebooks.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The module does not define any management objects. It defines only textual conventions that other MIB modules may use to define objects. The RFC says meaningful security considerations can only be written in the MIB modules that define management objects, so this document has no impact on the security of the Internet.

IANA assigned { mib-2 129 } to the VPN-TC-STD-MIB module.
sections.eli5: These are just empty boxes, not real data, so they cannot be attacked by themselves. Any real risk comes from the forms that use them.

fields.name: OUI
fields.desc: 3-octet Organizationally Unique Identifier of the VPN Authority.

fields.name: VPN index
fields.desc: 4-octet value assigned by the VPN Authority to identify the VPN within the OUI.
